creator: loganinthefuture
title: Review of 'Town' AI chief-of-staff app (~$20/mo): drafts email replies in your voice and escalates calendar decisions with one-tap approvals

tools.name: Town (AI chief of staff)
tools.detail: Free to paid tier 'about $20 a month'; drafts email replies, proposes calendar invites with yes/no notification

tools.name: Creator's own Claude-based chief-of-staff system
tools.detail: Hand-built over months; 'fixing my Claude system for the 17th time this week'

claims: Not sponsored; creator paid for the upgrade, roughly $20/month
Town 'nails your voice' in email draft replies better than expected
Escalates well: when someone proposed a 1:30 meeting, Town sent a notification 'I'm gonna send the invite if you're okay with that'; one tap and it handled the rest
Creator still has not calibrated it much
Was influenced by a creator on ChatGPT who did a four-part series on it
on_screen_only: Persistent caption 'I'm always skeptical ... But this tool gets an A' (talking head only)
cta: none (recommends following the other creator who did the series)

relevance.why: Email triage and calendar escalation are the exact admin load a solo founder wants off their plate; a cheap off-the-shelf tool may beat maintaining a home-built Claude chief-of-staff, which the creator admits is fragile.

implement_score.why: Low effort to trial at ~$20/mo, but it would duplicate an existing Claude-based email/calendar workflow; only worth it if that workflow is costing more than $20/mo of maintenance time.

verify: What is Town (vendor, URL, pricing tiers, which email/calendar providers it supports)?
Data access and privacy: it reads full inbox and calendar
Can it be driven from Claude Code / does it have an API, or is it a closed app?
Who is the 'four-part series' creator referenced?
